### Precise meaning via the universal cover

The integrand $(\log z)^2$ is multi-valued on $\mathbb{C}^*$, so the integral over $\Gamma$ is not defined in the ordinary sense. We lift the contour to the universal covering space $(\mathbb{C}, \exp)$, where $\exp:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}^*$, $w\mapsto e^w$, is the covering map. On the covering space the logarithm becomes the single-valued coordinate function $w$, so $(\log z)^2$ lifts to $w^2$.

Parametrize $\Gamma$ (counterclockwise, starting at $z=1$) by $z(t)=e^{it}$, $t\in[0,2\pi]$. The preimages of $z(0)=1$ under $\exp$ are $2\pi i k$, $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. The lift of $\Gamma$ starting at $w_0=2\pi i k$ is

$$\tilde\gamma_k(t)=2\pi i k + it,\qquad t\in[0,2\pi].$$

We **define** the integral by lifting:

$$\int_\Gamma (\log z)^2\,dz \;:=\; \int_{\tilde\gamma_k} w^2\,d(e^w)=\int_{\tilde\gamma_k} w^2 e^w\,dw.$$

Since $w=2\pi i k+it$, $dw=i\,dt$, $e^w=e^{it}$, this becomes

$$I_k=\int_0^{2\pi}(2\pi i k+it)^2\,e^{it}\,i\,dt.$$

### Evaluation

Set $a=2\pi i k$. Then $(a+it)^2=a^2+2ait-t^2$, so

$$I_k=i\Bigl[a^2\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!e^{it}dt+2ai\!\int_0^{2\pi}\!t\,e^{it}dt-\int_0^{2\pi}\!t^2 e^{it}dt\Bigr].$$

The three elementary integrals (integration by parts):

$$\int_0^{2\pi}e^{it}dt=0,\qquad \int_0^{2\pi}t\,e^{it}dt=\frac{2\pi}{i}=-2\pi i,$$

$$\int_0^{2\pi}t^2 e^{it}dt=\frac{4\pi^2}{i}-\frac{2}{i}\int_0^{2\pi}t\,e^{it}dt=-4\pi^2 i+4\pi=4\pi-4\pi^2 i.$$

Substituting, using $2ai\cdot(-2\pi i)=4\pi a=8\pi^2 i k$:

$$I_k=i\bigl[8\pi^2 i k-4\pi+4\pi^2 i\bigr]=-8\pi^2 k-4\pi i-4\pi^2.$$

Hence

$$\boxed{\,I_k=-4\pi^2(2k+1)-4\pi i,\qquad k\in\mathbb{Z}.\,}$$

### All possible values

The choice of lift is the only freedom, and it is indexed by $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. Therefore the set of all values that can be assigned to the integral is

$$\bigl\{\,-4\pi^2(2k+1)-4\pi i\;:\;k\in\mathbb{Z}\,\bigr\}=\bigl\{\,4\pi^2 m-4\pi i\;:\;m\text{ odd integer}\,\bigr\}.$$

The imaginary part is always $-4\pi i$; the real part ranges over all odd integer multiples of $4\pi^2$.
